newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms Torchmark, cut units' ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Torchmark, cut units' ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it had affirmed its ratings on Torchmark Corp. and Torchmark Capital L.L.C. and lowered its ratings on Torchmark's operating subsidiaries.

"These ratings have been removed from CreditWatch where they were placed February 2, 1996 following the company's announcement that management was exploring a strategic restructuring that could include dividing Torchmark into separate publicly traded operating companies," S&P said in a statement.
It said the long-term debt outlook was stable.
S&P said it took the following rating actions:
AFFIRMED AND REMOVED FROM CREDITWATCH
Torchmark Corp.
Issuer credit rating A
Senior debt rating A
Preferred stock rating A minus
Commercial paper rating A1
Torchmark Capital L.L.C
Preferred stock rating A minus
LOWERED AND REMOVED FROM CREDITWATCH
TO FROM
Globe Life & Accident Insurance Co.
Liberty National Life Insurance Co.
United American Insurance Co.
United Investors Life Insurance Co.
CPA AA AA plus
The rating agency also said it had the following expectations:
-- Torchmark's life premium will represent 70 percent of total premiums.
-- Liberty National will grow its life premium in the 2-4 percent range annually.
-- Liberty National's health premium will stabilise by 1997.
-- United American's premium income will stabilize by 1997.
-- Globe Life and Accident will experience premium growth of 8-10 percent annually.
-- United Investors' life premiums will grow around 10 percent annually.
-- American Income will experience premium growth in the 10-15 percent range annually.
-- Torchmark's pretax return on revenues will remain superior around 22 percent over the next few years.
-- Non-investment grade bonds will remain around 4-5 percent of the bond portfolio.
-- Mortgage-backed investments will continue to decline to around 20 percent of invested assets.
-- Torchmark will maintain debt leverage in the 30-40 percent range over the long-term.
-- Interest coverage will remain very good in the 7.0x-7.5x range.
-- Fixed charge coverage will remain in the 6.0x-6.5x range
-- Capital adequacy for the insurance subsidiaries will continue to decline, but will remain excellent.
-- The operating subsidiaries will upstream around 80 percent of net operating income as dividends.
-- Liquidity at the operating subsidiaries will remain excellent.
